curriculum.subject: Social Studies
curriculum.topic: Nigerian Geography: Regions, Climates & Major Cities
curriculum.subtopic: The 6 Geopolitical Zones and Vegetation Belts
objectives: Identify the six geopolitical zones of Nigeria on a map
Name major rivers (River Niger & River Benue) and where they meet (Lokoja confluence)
Describe the two main seasons in Nigeria: Rainy (Wet) and Dry (Harmattan) seasons
Locate key commercial and administrative cities: Abuja (FCT), Lagos, Kano, Port Harcourt, Enugu, and Ibadan
curriculum.lastWeekRevision: Last week we studied the physical features of our local government area, including hills, valleys, and local water streams.
curriculum.previousKnowledge: Pupils already know Nigeria has 36 states plus the Federal Capital Territory (Abuja) and have observed rainy and dry weather in their hometowns.

concreteVisualAids.title: Geopolitical Map of Nigeria
concreteVisualAids.description: Map showing North-Central, North-East, North-West, South-East, South-South, and South-West zones.
concreteVisualAids.caption: Nigeria with 6 Zones & 36 States

concreteVisualAids.title: The Y-Shaped River Confluence at Lokoja
concreteVisualAids.description: Where River Niger from Guinea highlands joins River Benue from Cameroon mountains to form the Y-shape.
concreteVisualAids.caption: Lokoja River Confluence

whiteboardSteps.title: 1. The 6 Geopolitical Zones of Nigeria
whiteboardSteps.teacherSpeech: Look at our country’s map. To govern and organize effectively, Nigeria is grouped into six geopolitical zones: North-West, North-East, North-Central, South-West, South-East, and South-South.
whiteboardSteps.boardText:
NIGERIA’S 6 GEOPOLITICAL ZONES

1. North-West (e.g. Kano, Kaduna, Sokoto)
2. North-East (e.g. Borno, Bauchi, Adamawa)
3. North-Central / Middle Belt (e.g. Plateau, Benue, Niger, FCT Abuja)
4. South-West (e.g. Lagos, Oyo, Ogun, Ondo)
5. South-East (e.g. Enugu, Anambra, Imo, Abia)
6. South-South / Niger Delta (e.g. Rivers, Delta, Akwa Ibom)
bulletPoints: 36 States + 1 Federal Capital Territory (Abuja)
Abuja is in North-Central and is the administrative capital
Lagos is in South-West and is the commercial nerve center

whiteboardSteps.title: 2. Major Rivers: Niger and Benue
whiteboardSteps.teacherSpeech: Two great rivers flow through Nigeria like arteries in the human body: River Niger (the longest) and River Benue. They meet at a historic junction called Lokoja in Kogi State. This meeting point forms a giant letter "Y" on the map!
whiteboardSteps.boardText:
THE GREAT RIVERS & CONFLUENCE

• River Niger: Enters from the North-West
• River Benue: Enters from Cameroon in the East
• Confluence City: LOKOJA (Kogi State)
• Flows South into: Atlantic Ocean through the Niger Delta Mangroves
bulletPoints: Confluence = Meeting point of two rivers
Kogi State is nicknamed "The Confluence State"
Provides fresh fish, fertile farmland, and water transportation
whiteboardSteps.equationOrHighlight: River Niger + River Benue = Lokoja Confluence (Y-Shape)

whiteboardSteps.title: 3. Climate and Two Main Seasons in Nigeria
whiteboardSteps.teacherSpeech: Unlike Europe where they have four seasons with winter snow, Nigeria experiences a tropical climate with two distinct seasons: The Rainy (Wet) Season and the Dry Season, which brings the cool, dusty Harmattan wind from the Sahara Desert.
whiteboardSteps.boardText:
OUR TWO SEASONS IN NIGERIA

🌧️ RAINY SEASON (April – October):
• Heavy rainfall, lush green vegetation
• Farmers plant yams, maize, cassava

☀️ DRY SEASON (November – March):
• High sunshine and warm days
• Harmattan wind (cool, dry, dusty breeze from the North)
bulletPoints: Southern coastal areas receive more rainfall
Northern savanna areas have longer dry seasons and sunny days
Harmattan brings dry skin and morning mist

practiceProblems.question: At which Nigerian city do River Niger and River Benue meet to form a famous confluence?
practiceProblems.concreteContext: Think of the state with the slogan "The Confluence State".
practiceProblems.explanation: River Niger and River Benue meet at Lokoja in Kogi State.

practiceProblems.question: Which geopolitical zone is home to the Federal Capital Territory (Abuja)?
practiceProblems.concreteContext: Abuja is located right near the center of Nigeria.
practiceProblems.explanation: Abuja is located in the North-Central geopolitical zone (also known as the Middle Belt).

assessmentQuestions.question: Which of the following states is correctly matched with its geopolitical zone?
assessmentQuestions.contextNigerian: Consider the regional grouping of Nigerian states.
assessmentQuestions.explanation: Rivers State (Port Harcourt) is in the South-South (Niger Delta) zone.
assessmentQuestions.hint: Rivers State is in the coastal oil-rich delta region of southern Nigeria.

assessmentQuestions.question: During which period of the year does Nigeria typically experience the dry Harmattan season?
assessmentQuestions.contextNigerian: Think about when dust from the Sahara and cool mornings occur around Christmas.
assessmentQuestions.explanation: The dry season and Harmattan wind blow between November and March.
assessmentQuestions.hint: It occurs during the dry months when skies are hazy and morning air is brisk.

assessmentQuestions.question: What letter does the confluence of River Niger and River Benue resemble on the map of Nigeria?
assessmentQuestions.contextNigerian: Look closely at how the two rivers flow from northwest and east down to the Atlantic.
assessmentQuestions.explanation: The two rivers meet at Lokoja and flow south together, forming the shape of a giant "Y".
assessmentQuestions.hint: It has two branches at the top merging into one stem below.

curriculum.contentOutline: Major Nigerian geopolitical zones, rivers Niger and Benue, seasonal climate variations.
learningActivities: Tracing River Niger and Benue meeting point at Lokoja

curriculum.subject: Mathematics
curriculum.topic: Whole Numbers & Place Value up to 100,000
curriculum.subtopic: Writing in Figures, Words & Expanded Notation
objectives: Count and write whole numbers up to 100,000 in figures and words
Identify the place value of any digit (Units, Tens, Hundreds, Thousands, Ten Thousands)
Expand numbers using place value decomposition (e.g. 48,250 = 40,000 + 8,000 + 200 + 50)
Solve real-world Nigerian money word problems involving Naira counting
curriculum.lastWeekRevision: In Primary 3, we mastered counting and place value up to 10,000 with cowries and base-10 blocks.
curriculum.previousKnowledge: Pupils know that 10 tens make 100, and 10 hundreds make 1,000, and can count ₦1000 notes.

concreteVisualAids.title: Naira Currency Bundle Chart
concreteVisualAids.description: Bundles of ₦1,000, ₦500, and ₦100 notes demonstrating place value.
concreteVisualAids.caption: 10 x ₦1,000 = ₦10,000 (Ten Thousand)

concreteVisualAids.title: Place Value Abacus Chart
concreteVisualAids.description: 5-spike abacus with beads for Units (U), Tens (T), Hundreds (H), Thousands (Th), and Ten Thousands (T.Th).
concreteVisualAids.caption: Place Value Columns: T.Th | Th | H | T | U

whiteboardSteps.title: 1. Understanding Place Value Columns
whiteboardSteps.teacherSpeech: Look at the number 54,321. Every digit has a house where it lives. From right to left: Units (1), Tens (10), Hundreds (100), Thousands (1,000), and Ten Thousands (10,000).
whiteboardSteps.boardText:
PLACE VALUE CHART:

[Ten Thousands] [Thousands] [Hundreds] [Tens] [Units]
       5              4          3        2       1

• 5 Ten Thousands = 50,000
• 4 Thousands     =  4,000
• 3 Hundreds      =    300
• 2 Tens          =     20
• 1 Unit          =      1
Total = Fifty-four thousand, three hundred and twenty-one.
bulletPoints: Always read digits in groups of three from right with a comma
54,321 has 5 Ten Thousands and 4 Thousands
Value of digit 4 is 4,000

whiteboardSteps.title: 2. Expanded Form with Nigerian Market Examples
whiteboardSteps.teacherSpeech: Imagine Mama Chidi sold 73,450 Naira worth of yams at Mile 12 Market. Let us break down this money: 70,000 + 3,000 + 400 + 50 + 0.
whiteboardSteps.boardText:
EXPANDED NOTATION:

₦73,450 =
7 Ten Thousands  (₦70,000)
+ 3 Thousands    (₦3,000)
+ 4 Hundreds     (₦400)
+ 5 Tens         (₦50)
+ 0 Units        (₦0)

Word Form: Seventy-three thousand, four hundred and fifty Naira.
bulletPoints: Zero in units column means no single Naira coins
Expanded form shows the true worth of each digit
In words, use hyphen for two-word numbers (seventy-three)

practiceProblems.question: What is the place value of the digit 7 in the number 87,412?
practiceProblems.concreteContext: Look at which column 7 sits in: T.Th, Th, H, T, or U.
practiceProblems.explanation: In 87,412, the digit 7 is in the Thousands column (worth 7,000).

practiceProblems.question: How do you write Sixty-five thousand and twenty in figures?
practiceProblems.concreteContext: Remember to place a zero in the Hundreds column!
practiceProblems.explanation: Sixty-five thousand and twenty is written as 65,020.

assessmentQuestions.question: In the number 94,832, what is the value of the digit 9?
assessmentQuestions.contextNigerian: Look at the highest column on the abacus.
assessmentQuestions.explanation: Digit 9 sits in the Ten Thousands column, so its value is 90,000.

assessmentQuestions.question: What is the expanded form of 42,608?
assessmentQuestions.contextNigerian: Notice there is a 0 in the Tens column.
assessmentQuestions.hint: Break each digit into its place value.

curriculum.contentOutline: Place value concepts up to 100,000 using Nigerian currency and concrete counters.
learningActivities: Grouping currency bundles into tens, hundreds, thousands

curriculum.subject: Mathematics
objectives: Identify the numerator (parts taken) and denominator (total equal parts)
Differentiate between Proper Fractions (3/4), Improper Fractions (5/3), and Mixed Numbers (1 2/3)
Convert improper fractions to mixed numbers using real-life food sharing
Compare like and unlike fractions visually
curriculum.lastWeekRevision: Last week we practiced whole numbers up to 100,000.
curriculum.previousKnowledge: Pupils know that sharing a whole orange into 2 equal halves gives 1/2 each, and 4 quarters gives 1/4 each.

concreteVisualAids.title: Loaf of Fresh Agege Bread
concreteVisualAids.description: A whole loaf sliced into 4 equal slices. 3 slices taken = 3/4.
concreteVisualAids.caption: 1 Whole Loaf = 4 Equal Slices (4/4)

concreteVisualAids.title: Sweet Nigerian Oranges
concreteVisualAids.description: Juicy oranges cut into 8 equal segments for sharing among siblings.
concreteVisualAids.caption: Fraction = Part / Whole

whiteboardSteps.title: 1. What is a Fraction?
whiteboardSteps.teacherSpeech: Nno nwam! When you buy a warm loaf of Agege bread from the bakery and slice it into 4 equal pieces, each piece is 1 part out of 4, written as 1/4.
whiteboardSteps.boardText:
ANATOMY OF A FRACTION:

   3  ← NUMERATOR (How many slices we have)
  --- 
   4  ← DENOMINATOR (Total equal slices in 1 whole loaf)

• Top Number (Numerator) = Parts taken
• Bottom Number (Denominator) = Total equal parts
bulletPoints: Denominator CANNOT be zero
Equal parts is mandatory (if slices are uneven, it is not a true fraction!)
4/4 = 1 whole loaf

whiteboardSteps.title: 2. The Three Types of Fractions
whiteboardSteps.teacherSpeech: There are 3 main types: Proper Fractions (small top), Improper Fractions (big heavy top), and Mixed Numbers (a whole number standing next to a fraction).
whiteboardSteps.boardText:
TYPES OF FRACTIONS:

1. PROPER FRACTION: Numerator < Denominator
   Example: 2/5, 3/4, 7/10 (Less than 1 whole)

2. IMPROPER FRACTION: Numerator ≥ Denominator
   Example: 5/3, 9/4 (Greater than 1 whole)

3. MIXED NUMBER: Whole Number + Proper Fraction
   Example: 1 2/3 (1 whole loaf + 2 extra slices)
bulletPoints: 5/3 means you have 5 slices, but 1 whole only takes 3 slices
So 5/3 is the exact same as 1 whole loaf and 2/3 of another loaf (1 2/3)

practiceProblems.question: Which of the following is an IMPROPER fraction?
practiceProblems.concreteContext: Look for the fraction where the top number (numerator) is bigger than the bottom.
practiceProblems.explanation: 9/5 has a numerator (9) larger than denominator (5), making it an improper fraction.

practiceProblems.question: Convert 7/3 into a mixed number.
practiceProblems.concreteContext: How many groups of 3 can you make out of 7? What is the remainder?

assessmentQuestions.question: In a basket of 10 mangoes, Tunde ate 3 mangoes. What fraction of the mangoes did Tunde eat?
assessmentQuestions.contextNigerian: Count the parts taken over the total mangoes in the basket.
assessmentQuestions.explanation: Tunde took 3 mangoes out of 10 total, which is 3/10.

assessmentQuestions.question: Which fraction is equivalent to 1/2?
assessmentQuestions.contextNigerian: Think of cutting an orange into 4 pieces and taking 2 pieces.
assessmentQuestions.explanation: 2/4 reduces to 1/2 by dividing both top and bottom by 2.
assessmentQuestions.hint: 2 slices out of 4 is half the loaf.

curriculum.contentOutline: Proper, improper and mixed fractions using Agege bread and agricultural produce.
learningActivities: Dividing Agege bread loaves into equal slices
Converting mixed numbers to improper fractions

curriculum.subject: Basic Science & Technology
curriculum.topic: Living & Non-Living Things in Our Environment
curriculum.subtopic: Characteristics of Living Organisms (MR NIGER D)
objectives: Distinguish between living and non-living things around the school and home compound
Recite the 7 fundamental characteristics of living things using the mnemonic MR NIGER D
Classify local examples: Goat, Neem tree, Cassava vs. Stone, Plastic bucket, Car
Explain why plants are living things even though they do not walk around
curriculum.lastWeekRevision: Last week we explored our school compound and drew a map of living plants and classroom furniture.
curriculum.previousKnowledge: Pupils know that a puppy barks and grows, while a toy car cannot eat or grow on its own.

concreteVisualAids.title: Nigerian Yard Organisms
concreteVisualAids.description: Living goat, mango tree, lizard alongside non-living clay pot and granite stones.
concreteVisualAids.caption: Living (Grows & Reproduces) vs. Non-Living

whiteboardSteps.title: 1. What Makes Something Alive?
whiteboardSteps.teacherSpeech: Good day! When you step into your compound in Enugu or Ibadan, you see goats, lizards, hibiscus flowers, and stones. How do we know which ones are alive? We use the golden Nigerian science code: MR NIGER D!
whiteboardSteps.boardText:
MR NIGER D - CHARACTERISTICS OF LIVING THINGS:

• M - Movement (Animals walk/run, plants bend towards sunlight)
• R - Respiration (Breathing in oxygen to release energy)
• N - Nutrition (Eating food: plants make food via sunlight)
• I - Irritability / Sensitivity (Reacting to touch, heat, cold)
• G - Growth (Getting bigger and taller over time)
• E - Excretion (Passing out waste materials)
• R - Reproduction (Having babies/seeds to make more of its kind)
• D - Death (All living things eventually die)
bulletPoints: Non-living things (like chairs, radios, rocks) cannot perform these functions
Plants are living because they grow, make food, breathe, and reproduce from seeds

practiceProblems.question: Which of the following is a LIVING thing?
practiceProblems.concreteContext: Which one can breathe, eat, and grow?
practiceProblems.explanation: A mango tree grows from a seed, produces fruits, and is a living organism.

assessmentQuestions.question: What does the letter "R" stand for in the MR NIGER D mnemonic for living things?
assessmentQuestions.contextNigerian: Think of breathing in air and producing offspring.
assessmentQuestions.explanation: The two Rs stand for Respiration (breathing) and Reproduction (producing young ones).
assessmentQuestions.hint: One is breathing, the other is making babies or seeds.

curriculum.contentOutline: Characteristics of living things vs non-living objects in Nigerian school and home environments.

curriculum.subject: English Studies
curriculum.subtopic: Identifying Naming Words in Nigerian Contexts
objectives: Define a noun as a naming word for a person, animal, place, or thing
Distinguish between Proper Nouns (capital letter: Nigeria, Aminat, Abuja) and Common Nouns (country, girl, city)
Recognize Collective Nouns (a herd of cattle, a flock of birds, a pride of lions)
Understand Abstract Nouns (honesty, happiness, courage - things you cannot touch)
curriculum.lastWeekRevision: Last week we revised parts of speech and phonics sounds.
curriculum.previousKnowledge: Pupils know their own names and names of objects in their classroom like pencil, desk, bag.

concreteVisualAids.title: Naming Word Basket
concreteVisualAids.description: Categorizing words into People (Doctor, Emeka), Places (Lagos, Market), and Things (Book, Drum).
concreteVisualAids.caption: Person | Place | Animal | Thing | Idea

whiteboardSteps.title: 1. The Four Types of Nouns
whiteboardSteps.teacherSpeech: Sannu kowa, good day! A noun is simply the name of anything. Let us explore the four important types you will encounter in Primary 4.
whiteboardSteps.boardText:
FOUR TYPES OF NOUNS:

1. PROPER NOUN: Specific name, ALWAYS starts with Capital Letter!
   • Nigeria, Lagos, Chidi, River Niger, Wednesday

2. COMMON NOUN: General name of persons, places, or things.
   • boy, teacher, hospital, football, yam

3. COLLECTIVE NOUN: Name for a group of things or people.
   • A herd of cattle (Fulani herdsmen)
   • A swarm of bees
   • A bouquet of flowers

4. ABSTRACT NOUN: Quality, feeling, or state you cannot physically touch.
   • Kindness, bravery, hunger, wisdom
bulletPoints: Always capitalize Proper Nouns wherever they appear in a sentence
Abstract nouns represent feelings and ideas (e.g. Joy, Peace)
whiteboardSteps.equationOrHighlight: Proper (Capital) vs Common (General) vs Collective (Group) vs Abstract (Feeling)

practiceProblems.question: Which word in this sentence is a PROPER noun? "Aminat travelled to Kano on Monday."
practiceProblems.concreteContext: Look for specific names that must always start with a capital letter.
practiceProblems.explanation: Aminat (person), Kano (city), and Monday (day) are specific names and thus Proper Nouns.

assessmentQuestions.question: What is the correct collective noun for a group of cows grazing together in the field?
assessmentQuestions.contextNigerian: Think of cattle moving together across the savanna.
assessmentQuestions.explanation: A group of cattle is called a "herd of cattle".
assessmentQuestions.hint: Sheep have flocks; cattle have herds.

curriculum.contentOutline: Proper, common, collective and abstract nouns with Nigerian community examples.
learningActivities: Identifying nouns in Nigerian folk story
Categorizing collective nouns like a herd of cattle

whiteboardSteps.title: 1. Skip Counting in 5s and 10s
whiteboardSteps.teacherSpeech: Nno nwam, good day! When you have a stack of ₦10 notes, you do not count 1, 2, 3... You count 10, 20, 30, 40, 50! This is skip counting.
bulletPoints: All numbers ending in 0 or 5 belong to the 5s family
Counting by 10s is fast for money calculation

assessmentQuestions.question: What is the next number after 25 when counting in 5s?
